decision: Wave51 is process-valid and establishes a replicated horizon boundary on 32 test episodes: for both replay-trained checkpoints, deployment-feasible current-buffer GAR is positive at horizon 2 (normalized edit-distance improvement 0.0824 and 0.0762), remains far above its matched target-free random control at horizon 5 (0.0271 and 0.0270 versus -0.4559), and selects a harmful fifth edit on average (-0.3125 and -0.28125 true advantage). Scale the paired horizon 2, 4, and 5 evaluations to 128 test episodes without training or checkpoint selection. Adopt horizon 4 as the fixed deployment-feasible operating point only if both checkpoints have positive normalized improvement at horizon 4, beat their matched random controls, and horizon 5 is worse than horizon 4; prefer horizon 2 if horizon 4 fails either checkpoint or does not improve on horizon 2. If the fifth-step decrement does not reproduce, do not claim a stable boundary and inspect episode-level uncertainty before further model changes. Candidate generation and GAR selection remain target-free; terminal targets are used only for separately labelled test metrics, and oracle-injected conditions remain candidate-privileged diagnostics.
